Friendly Feud Question 1/100

Friendly Feud Rules

×

Objective: Each question was previously asked to 100 people, and their most popular answers are hidden on the board. Two teams compete to guess those answers. Each answer is worth the number of people who gave that response. Eg: an answer given by 35 people is worth 35 points. After all rounds have been played, the team with the most points wins.

Set-up

  • Form 2 teams, preferably 5 or more members in each team.
  • # of rounds: Each question represents a round. The host can determine how many rounds the group wants to play.
  • Each round consists of a face-off followed by playing the board.

1. Face-off: Buzzer

  • Call one player from each team. Use different players for each Face-Off so everyone gets a chance to participate.
  • Reveal the survey question.
  • The first player to buzz gives an answer.

2. Face-off: Decide Who Gets Control

  • If the first player gives the #1 answer (the answer worth the highest points), their team immediately wins control.
  • If they give another answer on the board, the other player gets one chance to answer.
  • The player with the answer with more points wins control.
  • If both answers are worth the same points, the player who buzzed first wins.
  • If the first player gives an answer not on the board, the other player gets a chance.
  • If both players miss, continue asking alternating players from each team until someone gives an answer on the board.
  • Face-off misses do not count as strikes.

3. Face-off: Play or Pass

  • The team that wins the Face-Off chooses:
    • Play – their team tries to guess all the answers on the board.
    • Pass – the other team must play to guess all the answers on the board.

4. Playing the Board

  • Players on the controlling team answer one at a time in order. Players can’t help each other.
  • For each answer:
    • On the board: Reveal it and its points gets added to the round total.
    • Not on the board: Give the team 1 strike.
    • Already revealed: Give the team 1 strike.
  • Correct answers do not remove previous strikes.

5. Clearing the Board

If the playing team guesses every answer before getting 3 strikes, they win the round and receive all the points currently on the board.

6. Three Strikes

  • After the third strike: Give the other team one chance to steal. The stealing team may quickly discuss possible answers.
  • They must then give one final answer.
  • If their answer matches any unrevealed answer, they steal the round and receive the points. The stealing team only needs to guess one answer.
  • If their answer is wrong, the original playing team wins the round.

7. End of the Round

  • Add the round's points to the winning team's overall score.
  • Any answers still hidden can then be revealed, but their points are not added.
  • Only one team scores in each round.
  • Proceed to the next round’s face-off.

Winning

After the predetermined # of rounds, the team with the highest total score wins.

Host Reminders

  • Players do not need to say the exact wording on the board; accept answers that clearly mean the same thing.
  • Face-Off answers that are on the board remain revealed and count toward the round total.
